text.p: Lihir Gold Ltd said on Monday that it has sold forward 150,000 ounces of an anticipated 175,000 ounces of gold to be produced in 1997.
Andrew Vickerman, a director of Lihir, said production of the 175,000 ounces would commence when a plant for processing oxide ore was commissioned in May 1997.
In 1998, Lihir Gold expects to produce some 550,000 ounces as the sulphide ore reserves of the remote Papua New Guinea mine are tapped. Vickerman declined to detail the 1997 hedging plan.
The 1998 hedging programme, mainly in the form of put options, involves 150,000 ounces, the company said recently.
Under the terms of a US$300 million finance facility, Lihir Gold is required to ensure a certain minimum income from one-third of its projected production between 1998 and 2002.
The full programme ensures a guaranteed income of between US$422 and US$485 for about one million ounces from 1998 through 2002.

Lihir gold is owned 22.8 percent by Southern Gold, which is owned 75 percent by RTZ-CRA Ltd and 25 percent by Vengold Inc. Nuigini Mining Ltd owns 17.5 percent and the PNG government and landowners 17.5 percent.
